The design says 'the whole single-pair inner problem is a linear SPD system of only a few hundred DOF ... the angle-harmonics are the only nonlinear terms.' The design demotes k_axial*(L-r0) ('METRIC MEASURING THE WRONG THING #1') and promotes the Dirichlet anchor reaction as 'definitionally the force the boundary supplies and is independent of the GAP k_axial'. But the pinned FA node is a fiber END node with exactly ONE axial link plus a bending triple; force balance makes its reaction equal to minus that link's tension, i.e. exactly k_axial*(L01-r0_01) — the same quantity _sf_axial_tension computes at aleph/scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:158-167. M6's energy-ledger discriminator is mathematically impossible. With D defined as 'sum over inner iterations of F . dx measured along the ACTUAL displacement path' and W = sum(F_h*delta_abscissa_h), the closure is a PATH IDENTITY: for the total nodal force F, sum F.dx = -dU + W_motor along ANY path, converged or not, correct or not. So e = |W - (dU + D)|/W is ~0 always, the claimed discriminator ('if the solver is wrong the ledger does not close') is false, and the design's own rejection rule ('if e is flat in the budget, the ledger is tautological and must be rejected') would reject the nominal ledger. An independent U evaluator does not help because the tautology lives in D, not U. Fix: either drop the ledger, or replace D with a physically-defined dissipation against a real per-node drag gamma (which this slice does not model at all — sf_cytosol_transfer is excluded), and make the discriminator the RESIDUAL FORCE at the reported state, not energy closure.

M4's exact-limit criterion is false at the project's own constants. da_max = (f_stall - F)/k_xb (segment_motor.py:172, :223) with f_stall = 0.5 pN and k_xb = 1000 pN/um gives 0.50 nm/step, while tau*v0 with the driver default --dt 0.01 (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:284) and v0 = 0.12 um/s gives 1.20 nm. The cap is not a 'stall-crossing guard' — it is a per-step velocity clamp v_max = f_stall/(k_xb*tau) that overrides Hill for any dt > 4.17 ms, i.e. a lumped rate limiter sitting on top of the mechanistic Hill law. Either add dt < 4.17 ms as an explicit precondition of M4, or make the criterion v/v_eff where v_eff = min(v0, f_stall/(k_xb*tau)) and say so.

Analytic USEFUL bytes / event time yields achieved USEFUL bandwidth, and 10-15% of peak useful bandwidth is the expected signature of a BANDWIDTH-bound kernel with 4-32x sector amplification from uncoalesced access — indistinguishable from latency-bound. The design's stated control ('share one global reduction scalar → GATE 2 FAILS') therefore asserts a control will fire that provably will not. pi_questions: HARDWARE — probably the single largest lever in this track and not mine to decide. The solver is f64 everywhere (verified: 215 float64 sites in implicit_mechanics.py alone; the only f32 is the pruning-only hash-grid index). The RTX A5000 is GA102, which runs f64 at 1/64 of f32 (~0.43 TFLOPS f64, 768 GB/s, 16 GB); an A100 runs f64 at 1/2 (~9.7 TFLOPS, 1555 GB/s, 40-80 GB). If S0 shows the operator is f64-ALU-bound, a device change is worth more than every algorithmic lever in this document combined; if it is latency/occupancy-bound, it is still worth the bandwidth and SM count and it multiplies the ensemble R by 2.5-5x on memory alone. Question: is the project willing to move off the A5000 for sweep production, and does the hard rule 'the answer to native memory pressure is larger or multi-GPU hardware' extend to THROUGHPUT pressure?

SWEEP BUDGET — without this number, 'fast enough' is undefined and no optimisation can ever be declared DONE. Please state the target: how many cell types x how many cell states x how many replicates x how many physical seconds per run x acceptable wall per sweep. From that I can compute the required speedup and say honestly which combination of levers reaches it and which does not. Today's measured point is 0.05 s physical per 172 s wall, so the gap is currently ~4-6 orders of magnitude and the answer will certainly involve the surrogate — but the required factor determines whether S3+S7 alone could suffice for a reduced first sweep.

IS A HOST READBACK USED ONLY FOR LOOP CONTROL — no state read, no state mutation, bit-identical result — a violation of the zero-authoritative-GPU-to-CPU-roundtrip rule? This single ruling decides whether FIX1 can ship as written or must be re-implemented as a conditional graph. I recommend ruling it a violation anyway, because the conditional-graph implementation is strictly better (same skip, zero readback, fewer launches, guards still device-resident) — but the ruling is yours.

FIX2 CHANGES THE PRECONDITIONER on a solve that does NOT converge. A preconditioner change cannot move a CONVERGED fixed point, which is the usual reason preconditioner changes need no gate. But the production path is budget-exhausted (inner_iters = 400 = budget, inner_converged = False), so the emitted state IS preconditioner-dependent. Question: is a preconditioner change that alters a non-converged trajectory a gate-contract change requiring PI sign-off? The same question applies to S6's f32 preconditioner and is the reason I did not rank it higher.

IS A NEURAL SURROGATE ADMISSIBLE AT ALL under the fine-grained-mechanistic hard rule? A learned emulator is the most abstracted, most lumped object imaginable in a project whose first architectural principle is to prefer the mechanistic option even at higher cost. My proposed reconciliation is that the surrogate is not a runtime and not a model — it is a SEARCH POLICY over which native runs to perform, mechanically firewalled (package-level AST import ban, provenance gate blocking any production number without a native run id, native confirmation of every reported posterior point). But 'the surrogate explores, native decides' is a policy that needs your explicit ratification, not my inference, because it is the one place this track brushes against the project's founding rule.

DOES 'CO-LOCATION IS NEVER A CONNECTION' FORBID ensemble concatenation of independent cells into shared array sets even with a proven byte-identity block-diagonality gate? The letter of the rule is about physical connection within one cell; the spirit is that shared storage must never imply mechanical coupling. My reading is that a gated concatenation is admissible precisely because the gate proves non-coupling, and that stream-parallel separate cells (variant A) is the conservative fallback. Your call on whether the gate is sufficient.

PRECEDENT QUESTION on reduced precision: ac/solid/steric_warp.py:9-11,48-51 already builds the steric hash grid on an f32 copy of the positions, documented as safe because the grid only prunes far pairs while the force math stays f64. Is that (a) an accepted precedent that legitimises pruning-only reduced precision generally, or (b) something that needs retroactive gating? The answer sets the boundary for S6.

MAY I LAND S0 (profiler + throughput observable) NOW, ahead of the assembly tracks? It changes no physics, adds no constants, and is measurement-only — but it edits ac/cell/driver.py, which is feature-frozen (instrumentation is explicitly allowed, so I believe yes). The reason to do it now rather than after assembly is that every speedup estimate in this document is currently undecidable, and building the baseline incrementally as compartments land is far cheaper than reconstructing it cold at the end.

WHICH OBSERVABLE anchors the S7 dt-convergence plateau? A dt study needs one quantity to converge, and choosing it myself risks choosing one that is insensitive to dt and therefore produces a flat, vacuous plateau. I would propose the accepted-step force-balance residual plus one mechanical observable of the adherent configuration, but the choice is a measurement-protocol decision with gate consequences.
